EXPERIMENT 2: WORKING WITH DATA 
1. Importing Data from a Text File  
If we have a data in .txt, or .csv files we can import the data from those files treating them as a 
text files. Importing text or csv files into Excel creates a dynamic connection that allows you 
automate data cleaning and bypass standard row limits. It ensures data integrity by preventing 
Excel from auto-formatting values like dates or phone numbers. 
The steps for the importing data from the csv file are: 
Step 1- Open the notepad. 
Step 2- Write the data in the notepad that you want to import to the excel as shown below. 
 
Rules to follow while writing the csv file: 
i) One record per Line: Each row of data must stay on its own line, separated by line break and 
each data separated by comma. 
ii) Cons

he csv file: 
i) One record per Line: Each row of data must stay on its own line, separated by line break and 
each data separated by comma. 
ii) Consistent Column Count: Every row must have the exact same number of columns. if a 
row has missing data, leave it empty between the commas (e.g., Value1,  , Value2) rather than 
deleting the comma. 
iii) Header row: The first row should contain unique,  descriptive column name.  Avoid using 
special characters or spaces in headers 
iv)Save the file as .csv extension anywhere in your system.

1. Data Validation 
Data Validation is feature that allows you to control and restrict the type of data that can be 
entered into a cell. This ensures data accur acy, consistency, and reliability, which is crucial in 
data analytics. 
Data validation allows you to define rules or condition for the data that can be entered in a cell. 
These rules can include specifying acceptable values, numbers formats, text lengths, dates, or 
custom formulas. Data Validation helps prevent errors and inconsistencies in your dataset.

EXPERIMENT NO. 6  
Cleaning data containing date and time value: Use of DATEV ALUE function, DATEADD 
function, DATEDIF function, TIMEV ALUE function.  
Create columns like date, month, year and insert values.  
Create DOB column with: =DATE (C3, B3, A3) C3=year, B3=month, A3=date.  
1.DATEV ALUE:  
Date in the form of code numbers.  
First need to convert to text then use date value function.  
• Date format: =TEXT(D3,"MM-DD-YYYY")  
• Date value: =DATEV ALUE(E3)  
2.DATEADD:  
Adding required number of months, days, years.  
• Year add: =DATE(C3+4, B3, A3) C3=year, B3=month, A3=date  
• Month add: =DATE (C3, B3+4, A3)  
• Day add: =DATE(C3, B3, A3+4)  
 
3.DATEDIF:  
Used to calculate difference between 2 dates. Create today column and use =TODAY( ).  
• =DATEDIF(D3, G3,"Y"

add: =DATE(C3, B3, A3+4)  
 
3.DATEDIF:  
Used to calculate difference between 2 dates. Create today column and use =TODAY( ).  
• =DATEDIF(D3, G3,"Y") → calculating total no. of years from DOB to today.  
• =DATEDIF(D3, G3,"YM") → calculating total no. of months from DOB to today.  
• =DATEDIF(D3,G3,"MD") → calculating total no. of days from DOB to today.  
D3=DOB, G3=Today 
4.TIMEV ALUE: Time in the form of code numbers. Create hours, minutes, seconds columns. 
Convert it into time format: =TIME(N3,O3,P3) N3=hours, O3=MIN, P3=SEC. 
Convert to text: =TEXT(Q3,"HH:MM:SS") Q3=Time.  
Time value: =TIMEV ALUE(R3) R3=converted text of time
